A skyline drawing can make a city recognisable with only a few outlines. Towers, roofs and unusual profiles provide cues. Yet the result is a strong ____1____ of the place, not a complete account. Many ordinary buildings disappear into one continuous shape. Streets, interiors and people are mostly ____2____. The drawing succeeds by selecting features useful for recognition. Misrepresentation begins when the image is asked to ____3____ more than it shows. A familiar outline can represent a city without describing its everyday ____4____. Its value depends on understanding the kind of ____5____ it makes.

Viewpoint matters. The same buildings can overlap differently when seen from another position. A distant tower may appear beside a roof that is actually far away from it. The two forms are neighbours in the ____6____, not necessarily on the ground. Scale changes too: details visible nearby disappear at a distance, while a large profile remains. A designer may simplify further to make a symbol readable at a small ____7____. Such changes need not be errors if the purpose is a recognisable mark. They would be problems in a drawing intended to give precise ____8____. A symbol and a survey can share a subject while serving different ____9____. Comparing them requires attention to that ____10____.

The familiar skyline may also change over time. A new structure can alter the profile, while an old logo preserves a previous view. That does not make the older image meaningless. It can become a record of what was once selected as characteristic. A date helps viewers place it. Without them, a historical symbol may be mistaken for a current ____11____. Clear description prevents one useful image from carrying the wrong claim. The question is not whether simplified pictures should be used. It is whether their selection, viewpoint and date suit the job. A good outline can communicate quickly because it leaves much ____12____. Responsible use keeps that economy from becoming a false promise of completeness. We can enjoy recognition while asking what the image cannot ____13____. The city continues beyond the line, with a complexity no single profile could ____14____. The outline is an entrance to the subject, not its final ____15____.
